role_in_parent: This is the new core combinatorial lemma replacing the rejected false reconstruction lemma based on the least-admissible-coordinate map.
statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2 and let g be an integer with g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i + j < m then x_i + x_j >= x_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then x_i + x_j + 1 >= x_{i+j-m}, and such that x_1 + ... + x_{m-1} = g. Define K_{m,g+1} analogously with coordinate sum g+1. Then there exists an injective function J_{m,g} from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}.

domain_restrictions: m is an integer with m ≥ 2
g is an integer with g ≥ 0
x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) has all coordinates x_k ∈ Z_{>0} (positive integers)
x satisfies the coordinate sum constraint: x_1 + ... + x_{m-1} = g
in the defining inequalities, i and j range over all ordered pairs with i,j ∈ {1,...,m-1}
for i+j<m: inequality uses x_{i+j} (which lies in {1,...,m-1})
for i+j>m: inequality uses x_{i+j-m} (which lies in {1,...,m-1})
K_{m,g+1} is defined by the same conditions with x_1+...+x_{m-1}=g+1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer m ≥ 2 and every integer g ≥ 0, there exists a function J_{m,g} mapping each x ∈ K_{m,g} (i.e., each positive integer (m−1)-tuple with sum g and satisfying the given conditional inequalities for all i,j∈{1,...,m−1}) into K_{m,g+1} (same constraints but sum g+1), such that for all x,y ∈ K_{m,g}, x ≠ y implies J_{m,g}(x) ≠ J_{m,g}(y).

variables.name: m
variables.role: global parameter controlling tuple length {1,...,m-1} and split in inequalities

variables.name: g
variables.role: global parameter fixing the required coordinate sum of elements of K_{m,g}

variables.name: x
variables.role: arbitrary element of K_{m,g} with coordinates x_1,...,x_{m-1}

variables.name: i
variables.role: index used in defining the pairwise inequality constraints

variables.name: j
variables.role: index used in defining the pairwise inequality constraints

variables.name: J_{m,g}
variables.role: witness for the existence of an injective mapping from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}

witness_dependencies: The function witness J_{m,g} is allowed to depend on the parameters (m,g).
The injectivity condition depends on the membership relation x,y ∈ K_{m,g}.
